title: Ticking Internal customer and saving flags the customer with a badge
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A with no open work orders.
custom_steps:
1. Open customer A's page.
  2. Click Edit Customer on customer A's page.
  3. Tick the "Internal customer" checkbox.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Open the Customers list.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The customer header shows no "Internal" badge.

Step 2:

  • The Edit Customer window opens.

Step 3:

  • "Default internal category" appears with "General Internal".

Step 4:

  • The window closes with no Make internal window, since customer A has no open work orders.
  • The customer header shows an "Internal" badge next to customer A's name.

Step 5:

  • Customer A's row shows the "Internal" badge next to its name.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R7: “Edit Customer shows the checkbox "Internal customer" as the last field of the dialog, below "PO is required", with the helper "Work orders for this customer are internal: no prices, no invoice, parts cost posts to the expense account of the internal category." When ticked, the select "Default internal category" appears under it, listing the active Internal categories, General Internal preselected. It is shown while the setting is on (S1-N4 for the exception). New Customer does not show it: a customer is flagged after it exists, from Edit Customer or the modal. The checkbox and the modal are the only places the flag is set; ticking it on Save flags the customer (with the dialog of S1-R11 when open billable work orders exist).”
  • S1-R8: “While the setting is on, a flagged customer shows an "Internal" badge next to its name in the customer header, in the customers list and on the customers list mobile card. While the setting is off the badge is hidden in all three places (S1-N4); the badges on work orders stay (S2-R10).”
  • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions (Action | Needs | Without it): “See the Internal badge on the customers list and the customer header | Customers page access | Not applicable”
  • Terminology: “Internal customer → one of the shop's existing customers flagged as the shop's own company or a sister company. Set in the modal that opens the first time the setting is switched on, or at the bottom of Edit Customer; nowhere else. Several allowed. Not a system customer: ShopView creates nothing.”
  • Feature Overview: “Internal work orders come from internal customers. The shop flags its own company (and any sister company) as an internal customer once: in the modal that opens the first time the Internal Work Orders setting is switched on (nobody is preselected: the location is not necessarily a customer and the names differ), or later with the Internal customer checkbox at the bottom of Edit Customer. Settings > Work Orders holds the toggle, that one-time modal and two hints: a link to the categories page and a link to the QuickBooks mapping. Every internal customer carries a default internal category, General Internal unless changed on Edit Customer; an asset of an internal customer can carry its own category (Edit Asset). A new internal work order takes the asset's category, else the customer's, else General Internal. Nobody picks a category or an account on the work order; the Internal badge and its tooltip say where it posts.”
